accepted_claims.statement: Selected B files start without a comment header and their first record has seven fields. The current BRASS B parser consumes eleven fields, as does the current RUSTICO writer. This is a verified format distinction; it does not supply a conversion or prove whole-file validity. Prior released seven-field semantics remain conditional context.

Current cut-sky source assigns product weights and distinguishes active DATA/RANDOM readers from commented Patchy alternatives; selected output branches subtract monopole/B shot noise and carry explicit normalization/mix choices. An exact catalogue parser and run configuration are required before mapping a released mock to this implementation.

The current auto-RR code selects midpoint or one-endpoint LOS, forms weighted even Legendre moments with separation factors and divides by a selected W0 bin, searching later bins when zero. This normalization is conditionally interpretable when the denominator and pair-mean bins are valid; source guard behavior and realized validity are unqualified. Its seven-field writer puts the bin center before pair-mean separation, although the literal header names them in the opposite order. The current BRASS reader treats them as sav then seff. No source repair or legacy squared-mask equivalence is accepted.

BRASS declares configurable covariance corrections, shot-noise/window treatment and fitted model/σ8 options. These are configuration choices, not the frozen historical parameterization, an observed statistical law, independence or qualified amplitudes.

Selected current covariance source builds a common vector and accumulates residual products divided by Ncounter−1 and a scaling factor; P/B successful-file counters are separate and only total equality is checked at the selected refusal. Equal counts alone do not establish identical valid realization-ID sets. All covariance values, inverse law, correction validity and likelihood remain unexecuted/unqualified.
